methodology: Verbatim article paragraphs are sent to minimax-m3 (via ollama-cloud) for structured spec extraction. The LLM is asked to identify the team's specific technical specification or design change for each (team, part) pair. Specs are rejected if the LLM's confidence is below 0.35, if the spec text doesn't mention the team or the part, or if the article text doesn't actually support the claim. (team, part) pairs without a valid spec are simply absent from the output. The page falls back to the regulation-level INTERPRETATION_DEFAULT for those pairs.

specs.spec: Alpine uses an inverted rear wing, allowing airflow to follow and compress against the wing rather than being abruptly interrupted under DRS, theoretically increasing downforce.
Alpine opted for bulky sidepods with a large sidepod inlet and less centreline cooling than the Racing Bulls design.
Aston Martin’s nose has a notably wide, broad front section.
Aston Martin receives Honda's own 2026-spec power unit under an exclusive works-team agreement, following the end of Honda's relationship with Red Bull Racing.
Audi enters Formula One as a works team in 2026 using its own power unit.

Cadillac's front wing is described as conservative and close to the FIA show car, with differently shaped endplates and outermost elements appearing to outwash rather than point in the opposite direction as on the RB22 render.
The Cadillac's sidepod intakes resemble those of the Ferrari F1-75 but feature a slight underbite, while the rear of the sidepod uses ramp geometry reminiscent of 2012-13 F1 cars.
Leclerc will adopt Lewis Hamilton's brake configuration for Barcelona to address the Ferrari's inconsistent braking and unpredictable corner-to-corner behavior.

source.author: Josh Suttill, Jon Noble, Jack Cozens, Scott Mitchell-Malm

specs.spec: The SF-26 appears to feature a hole in its rear diffuser, similar to the Mercedes rear-diffuser treatment. It is speculated that this may be an early A-Spec car intended for Spain testing.
The 2026 Scuderia Ferrari car is listed as using a Ferrari V6 turbo power unit.
Ferrari's front suspension and brake ducts were described as being similar to those of Mercedes.
Haas uses the Ferrari engine and gearbox, but not the Ferrari gearbox casing or rear suspension.
The Haas sidepods feature very large inlet openings and generally chunky sidepod bodywork.
The rear suspension was described as a non-Ferrari, Haas-specific component rather than Ferrari's, despite the car using a Ferrari engine and gearbox; the gearbox casing was also non-Ferrari.
McLaren appears to carry forward its 2025 sidepod design and philosophy, with a more aggressive ramp down into the diffuser.
McLaren's 2026 sidepods appear to retain the 2025 sidepod design philosophy, while adopting a more aggressive ramp down toward the diffuser.

Mercedes is said to exploit a front-wing flap regulation loophole, using the permitted FW-profile rotation range to double the available transition duration when moving the flap between straight and corner modes.
Mercedes supplies its power units to Alpine for the 2026 season, replacing Renault's engine-supplier role with the Alpine team.
VCARB's front-wing rendering shows four moving flaps with two actuators, apparently using a front-hinged flap arrangement that would fail the Straight Mode test.
Albon managed the Red Bull's battery energy deployment to compensate for the Honda's limited recharge capability, but a deployment issue remained and cost the car engine braking.

source.author: Josh Suttill, Jon Noble, Jack Cozens, Scott Mitchell-Malm

specs.spec: Williams' rear suspension does not use push-rod or pull-rod linkages; the team has stated that the front suspension will use pull-rods.
